purpose: Adds a cross-session trends view to Lumen so a user can see how cost, cache hit ratio, turn count, and anomaly rate are changing across their own tracked sessions over time, and, for Claude Code specifically, how compaction behavior (frequency, tokens dropped, auto-vs-manual trigger split) is changing -- exposed as a new `lumen trends` CLI subcommand that reads raw per-session metrics with no statistical shift-detection and no cause attribution.
scope: Covers: (1) a new `lumen trends` subcommand in crates/lumen-cli, following the existing synchronous, store-backed command pattern (trace/audit/ingest/sessions/session); (2) a new CompactionEvent domain-model surface on CanonicalTranscript in crates/lumen-model, populated by ClaudeCodeAdapter from the real `compact_boundary` system event's `compactMetadata` (trigger, preTokens, postTokens, cumulativeDroppedTokens, durationMs), plus a `sequence` field recording each event's 0-based transcript encounter order; (3) persistence of one compaction fact record per parsed compact_boundary event, keyed by the internal sessions.id foreign key and written inside SessionRepository::upsert_session's existing atomic transaction via a new CompactionRepository (delete_for_session + insert_compaction_facts) backed by a new `compaction_events` table declared explicitly in crates/lumen-store/src/migrations.rs, following the same pattern already used for token_usage and tool_calls (CRIT-LUMEN-177) -- not a separate write path outside that transaction; (4) a trend query path over the existing `sessions` table (and the new compaction facts table) computed fresh at request time, including a store-wide TrendRepository::count_sessions query used to make CRIT-LUMEN-188's zero-Claude-Code-sessions check independent of --limit -- see reasoning for why this spec does not extend RollupRepository. Does not cover live/streaming updates, threshold alerting, statistical change-point detection, or cause attribution -- see non_goals.
non_goals: No statistical shift-detection of any kind (CUSUM, PELT, z-score, or any other change-point method) -- the trend view presents raw per-session and set-level metrics for the user to read and interpret themselves, not an alerting or classification system.

No attribution of a trend or shift to a cause (e.g. correlating a cost increase with a model change or a plugin update) -- this requires sparse plugin/MCP-state capture that does not exist in Lumen today and is deferred to a later requirement.

No extension of RollupRepository and no new rollup-population job in this spec -- RollupRepository is fully coded but deliberately unwired (CRIT-LUMEN-174, SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE), its schema is economic/volume-only, and adding behavioral aggregates plus a periodization/population pipeline to an already-unused component is more surface than a v1 read-only trend view justifies. Trends are computed via fresh queries over the `sessions` table (and the new compaction facts table) at request time instead.

No compaction metrics for Codex, Antigravity, or OpenCode sessions -- compaction (compact_boundary) is a Claude Code-specific transcript event with no equivalent captured from the other three orchestrators today. Those providers get cost/cache-hit-ratio/turn-count/anomaly-rate trends only.
No real-time or live-updating trend view -- `lumen trends` computes and renders a snapshot on each invocation, matching every other Lumen CLI command; it does not stream or watch for new sessions.
No threshold alerting or notifications -- the trend view is passive and read-only; it never pushes a notification or triggers an external action.

api_surface.name: Commands::Trends
api_surface.signature: Trends { #[arg(long)] provider: Option<String>, #[arg(long, default_value_t = 50)] limit: usize, #[arg(long)] compaction: bool }
api_surface.description: New clap subcommand variant on the existing `Commands` enum in crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs, alongside Trace/Audit/Ingest/Sessions/Session. --provider filters to one provider string (matching sessions' convention: claude-code, codex, antigravity, opencode); omitted, all providers included. --limit caps the trend set (same semantics as `lumen sessions --limit`, default 50) -- see CRIT-LUMEN-190. --compaction additionally requests Claude Code compaction metrics. Respects existing --json/--db global flags.

api_surface.name: cmd_trends
api_surface.signature: fn cmd_trends(db_path: &Utf8PathBuf, provider: Option<String>, limit: usize, compaction: bool, json_mode: bool) -> Result<()>
api_surface.description: Handler for Commands::Trends: opens the store, applies --provider filter then --limit cap (CRIT-LUMEN-190), evaluates the 2-session minimum (CRIT-LUMEN-187) and --compaction error cases (CRIT-LUMEN-188, CRIT-LUMEN-189), renders oldest-to-newest, computes set-level anomaly rate, outputs table (comfy-table) or JSON (CRIT-LUMEN-186). Table columns: Provider, Session ID, Started At, Cost USD, Cache Hit %, Turns, Anomalies, plus (when --compaction) Compaction Count, Tokens Dropped, Auto/Manual, formatted per CRIT-LUMEN-183.

api_surface.name: TrendRepository::list_session_trend
api_surface.signature: pub fn list_session_trend(&self, filter: &TrendFilter) -> Result<Vec<SessionTrendPoint>, StoreError>; pub struct TrendFilter { pub provider: Option<String>, pub limit: usize, pub require_compaction: bool }; pub struct SessionTrendPoint { pub provider: String, pub session_id: String, pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>, pub cost: Cost, pub cache_hit_ratio: f32, pub turn_count: usize, pub has_anomalies: bool, #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub compaction: Option<CompactionSummary> }
api_surface.description: New repository in crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/trend.rs, alongside SessionRepository (deliberately not RollupRepository, see reasoning). LEFT JOINs the compaction facts table when require_compaction is set (non-Claude-Code sessions must still appear -- CRIT-LUMEN-184), filters by provider, caps to `limit` most recent by started_at desc (ties by provider_session_id asc), returns re-ordered oldest-to-newest. Returns empty Vec when nothing matches; CLI owns CRIT-LUMEN-187, count_sessions owns CRIT-LUMEN-188. require_compaction, when true, populates .compaction for every Claude Code session regardless of whether it has events; never affects selection. .compaction is None when require_compaction is false OR provider != claude-code (and, per CRIT-LUMEN-186, the `compaction` key is then omitted from JSON output entirely via #[serde(skip_serializing_if)], never emitted as null); Some(zeros) for a Claude Code session with zero events; Some(real counts) otherwise -- so zero-events and not-applicable are always distinguishable by provider, never collapsed.

api_surface.name: TrendRepository::count_sessions
api_surface.signature: pub fn count_sessions(&self, provider: &str) -> Result<usize, StoreError>
api_surface.description: Store-wide SELECT COUNT(*) against sessions filtered by provider, no --limit applied -- backs CRIT-LUMEN-188, evaluated before the --limit cap so the check reflects the whole store, not just the visible --limit window.

api_surface.name: CompactionSummary
api_surface.signature: pub struct CompactionSummary { pub event_count: usize, pub tokens_dropped_total: u64, pub auto_count: usize, pub manual_count: usize }
api_surface.description: tokens_dropped_total is the cumulative_dropped_tokens of the session's LAST PERSISTED compaction event by sequence order (CRIT-LUMEN-184) -- never summed; 'last' means highest sequence actually present in compaction_events, since sequence can have gaps from CRIT-LUMEN-192-skipped events.

api_surface.name: CompactionEvent
api_surface.signature: pub struct CompactionEvent { pub sequence: u32, pub trigger: CompactionTrigger, pub pre_tokens: u64, pub post_tokens: u64, pub cumulative_dropped_tokens: u64, pub duration_ms: u64 } pub enum CompactionTrigger { Auto, Manual }
api_surface.description: New domain type in lumen-model/src/transcript.rs; CanonicalTranscript gains compaction_events: SmallVec<[CompactionEvent; 4]>. ClaudeCodeAdapter parses each compact_boundary event; sequence is 0-based transcript encounter order, assigned by the adapter.

api_surface.name: CompactionFactRecord persistence
api_surface.signature: pub struct CompactionFactRecord { pub session_id: i64, pub sequence: u32, pub trigger: String, pub pre_tokens: u64, pub post_tokens: u64, pub cumulative_dropped_tokens: u64, pub duration_ms: u64 }
api_surface.description: Keyed by internal sessions.id FK, matching SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE's established pattern. cmd_ingest builds these onto SessionFactRecord.compaction_events.

api_surface.name: SessionFactRecord::compaction_events
api_surface.signature: pub struct SessionFactRecord { pub tool_calls: Vec<ToolCallFactRecord>, pub compaction_events: Vec<CompactionFactRecord> }
api_surface.description: New field, populated alongside tool_calls, flowing through upsert_session's existing transaction.

api_surface.name: CompactionRepository
api_surface.signature: impl<'a> CompactionRepository<'a> { pub fn delete_for_session(&self, session_id: i64) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn insert_compaction_facts(&self, session_id: i64, events: &[CompactionFactRecord]) -> Result<(), StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Invoked by SessionRepository::upsert_session inside its existing atomic transaction, alongside token_usage_repo/tool_call_repo -- delete-then-reinsert, matching CRIT-LUMEN-177's pattern.

api_surface.name: Migration: compaction_events table
api_surface.signature: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS compaction_events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, session_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, sequence INTEGER NOT NULL, trigger TEXT NOT NULL, pre_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL, post_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL, cumulative_dropped_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL, duration_ms INTEGER NOT NULL); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_compaction_events_session ON compaction_events(session_id);
api_surface.description: New migration in crates/lumen-store/src/migrations.rs, declared explicitly alongside sessions/token_usage/tool_calls, using IF NOT EXISTS on both statements -- required because MigrationManager::SCHEMA is re-executed in full on every SqliteStore::open, matching every existing table/index in this schema.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN `lumen trends` is executed with no --provider filter and at least 2 sessions in the store match the filter, THE SYSTEM SHALL render, for each matching session ordered oldest-to-newest by started_at, its cost (or an explicit "unknown" for an unpriced model, never a fabricated figure), cache hit ratio, and turn count, plus one set-level anomaly rate figure: (count of sessions in the returned set with has_anomalies = true / total sessions in the returned set) * 100.0, i.e. a percentage in [0.0, 100.0], the same scale convention as cache_hit_ratio (see below) -- NOT a [0.0, 1.0] fraction. In TABLE mode specifically: cache hit ratio SHALL be taken directly from the stored sessions.cache_hit_ratio value, which is already a percentage in [0.0, 100.0] (see crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs, crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs's existing `format!("{:.1}%", ...)` renderer) -- rounded half-to-even to one decimal place and rendered with a trailing "%", NEVER multiplied by 100 again; turn_count SHALL be formatted as a plain non-negative integer; the set-level anomaly rate SHALL be rounded half-to-even to one decimal place and rendered with a trailing "%", using the same rounding rule as cache hit ratio (both are already percentages in [0.0, 100.0] at this point, so both round the same way).

WHEN `lumen trends --compaction` is executed (whether or not --provider is set) and at least 1 Claude Code session is present in the returned trend set, THE SYSTEM SHALL render, per Claude Code session, its compaction event count, its total tokens dropped by compaction (computed as the cumulativeDroppedTokens value of that session's LAST persisted compaction event by sequence order -- since cumulativeDroppedTokens is already a running total, it SHALL NOT be summed across events), and the count of auto-triggered versus manual-triggered compactions for that session -- a Claude Code session with zero persisted compaction events shows a count of 0 and a tokens-dropped figure of 0, not an omitted row. IF a session's highest-sequence compact_boundary event was skipped per CRIT-LUMEN-192, tokens_dropped_total SHALL be computed from the highest-sequence event that WAS persisted for that session, never silently substituted from an earlier, lower-sequence event chosen for convenience. WHEN --compaction is set with no --provider filter, non-Claude-Code sessions in the trend set SHALL render an explicit not-applicable marker (table: "n/a"; JSON: the compaction key absent per CRIT-LUMEN-186), never a zero-valued compaction object.

WHEN `lumen ingest` parses a Claude Code session file containing one or more `compact_boundary` system events, THE SYSTEM SHALL persist one compaction fact record per event, each capturing sequence (0-based transcript encounter order), trigger, preTokens, postTokens, cumulativeDroppedTokens, and durationMs exactly as present in that event's compactMetadata, queryable back from the store afterward. sequence increments for every compact_boundary event encountered, including ones later skipped per CRIT-LUMEN-192, so persisted sequence values may have gaps. WHEN `lumen ingest` re-parses a session file for a (provider, provider_session_id) already present, THE SYSTEM SHALL delete all existing compaction fact records for that session's internal sessions.id before inserting the newly parsed set -- inside the same atomic transaction as upsert_session's own writes (CRIT-LUMEN-177).

WHEN `lumen trends` is executed with --json, THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a JSON object (not a bare array -- a bare array cannot also carry a sibling set-level field) with two top-level members: "sessions", an array ordered oldest-to-newest by started_at with one entry per session -- provider, session_id, started_at (RFC 3339), cost as `{"usd": <f64>, "priced": true}` or `{"usd": null, "priced": false}` (Cost currently has no Serialize impl; adding one producing this shape is part of this spec), cache_hit_ratio as a plain JSON number in [0.0, 100.0] -- the stored sessions.cache_hit_ratio percentage (see CRIT-LUMEN-183), rounded half-to-even to one decimal place before serializing, NOT a [0.0, 1.0] fraction and NOT the raw unrounded f32 value -- turn_count, has_anomalies, and -- ONLY when --compaction was set -- a compaction object for Claude Code sessions or, for other providers, no compaction key at all (the key SHALL be absent, never present as null, when --compaction is not set on the whole invocation, and absent specifically for non-Claude-Code rows even when --compaction is set); and "anomaly_rate", a top-level plain JSON number in [0.0, 100.0] computed and rounded exactly as defined in CRIT-LUMEN-183 -- the same percentage scale and rounding as cache_hit_ratio, not a [0.0, 1.0] fraction. This deliberately diverges from `lumen sessions --json`'s bare-array output, which has no set-level field to carry.

IF, after applying the --provider filter and the --limit cap per CRIT-LUMEN-190, fewer than 2 sessions remain, THE SYSTEM SHALL return a clear error stating at least 2 sessions are required, rather than rendering a degenerate table/JSON or panicking. Concretely: `lumen trends --limit 1` against 10 matching sessions SHALL also error.

IF `lumen trends --compaction` is executed with no --provider filter, or --provider explicitly "claude-code", THE SYSTEM SHALL check TrendRepository::count_sessions("claude-code") -- evaluated before --limit -- and IF zero, return a clear error stating no Claude Code sessions are available for compaction data, rather than rendering an empty/all-zero section or panicking.

IF `lumen trends --compaction` is executed with --provider set to a value other than "claude-code", THE SYSTEM SHALL return a clear error naming the incompatible provider, rather than silently ignoring either flag. This check takes precedence over CRIT-LUMEN-188 whenever both would apply.

WHEN `lumen trends --limit <n>` is executed, THE SYSTEM SHALL apply --provider first, THEN restrict to at most n most recent matching sessions by started_at descending (ties by provider_session_id ascending), and only THEN evaluate CRIT-LUMEN-187 and compute figures -- matching `lumen sessions --limit`'s filter-then-cap ordering, and additionally introducing a tie-break `list_recent` does not have today. A --limit of 0 SHALL be coerced to 50, matching `list_recent`'s existing behavior.

WHEN `lumen trends` is executed in any mode, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT emit any derived statistical shift-detection signal (no CUSUM/PELT/z-score, no classification, no trend-direction label) and SHALL NOT attribute any change to a cause -- output is limited to raw per-session metrics and the set-level anomaly-rate figure from CRIT-LUMEN-183.

IF a compact_boundary event's compactMetadata is missing, OR any of trigger/preTokens/postTokens/cumulativeDroppedTokens/durationMs is absent (confirmed against real local Claude Code data: cumulativeDroppedTokens absent from compactMetadata in 17 of 112 real compact_boundary events independently verified this session, ~15%), OR trigger is neither "auto" nor "manual", OR any numeric field fails to parse as a non-negative integer, THE SYSTEM SHALL skip persisting a record for that event, record it as a parse failure per CRIT-LUMEN-025, and continue ingesting the session's remaining events/lines. Note: this means CRIT-LUMEN-184's compaction event_count and auto/manual counts under-report true compaction frequency by roughly this same fraction for any session containing such events -- an accepted, documented limitation of parsing only well-formed events, not a defect.

linked_research: none -- internal-only trace pass, no external research report produced
reasoning: RollupRepository-vs-fresh-query decision: chose fresh queries over the `sessions` table (plus a new compaction facts table), not an extension of RollupRepository. RollupRepository is fully coded (crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/rollup.rs) but was deliberately left unwired per CRIT-LUMEN-174/SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE -- nothing populates it today. Its schema (period_start, period_type, session_count, total_cost_usd, total_savings_usd, total_duration_ms) is purely economic/volume; serving this feature through it would require a schema migration, an invented periodization policy, and a population job -- three new pieces of unproven, currently-dead machinery. A direct TrendRepository query, computed fresh on each invocation, matches the existing architecture exactly (every existing CLI command is a synchronous, on-demand, direct-query command) and can be revisited to route through RollupRepository later if real usage shows the fresh-query path is too slow. Compaction domain-model gap: verified against real local Claude Code data that CanonicalTranscript has no field for this today, so CompactionEvent/CompactionTrigger are new, minimal additions mirroring the existing TrajectoryAnomaly pattern. CLI shape verified directly against crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs and SPEC-LUMEN-008-CLI: `trends` follows the exact Commands-enum-variant-plus-cmd_* handler pattern of the other five commands, reuses --json/--db, and reuses `sessions`'s --provider/--limit conventions. Filter/limit/minimum ordering: --provider applied before --limit, --limit applied before CRIT-LUMEN-187's 2-session minimum, so the minimum check always reflects what would actually render and --limit cannot dodge it. Persistence design: CompactionFactRecord is keyed by the internal sessions.id FK, not provider_session_id, and written inside SessionRepository::upsert_session's existing atomic transaction via CompactionRepository -- matching the pattern already established for token_usage and tool_calls; keying by provider_session_id or writing outside that transaction would reopen exactly the partial-write risk CRIT-LUMEN-177 closed. Store-wide Claude Code count for CRIT-188: list_session_trend only returns rows within the --limit window, so it cannot distinguish store-wide zero from window-zero; count_sessions is a separate store-wide query run before --limit is applied. Cost JSON representation: no existing Serialize convention for Cost exists anywhere in the workspace today (Cost has no Serialize impl); `lumen sessions --json` instead serializes SessionSummaryReadModel's flat total_cost_usd + is_fully_priced fields directly, a different representation of the same underlying data -- this spec's {"usd", "priced"} shape is a new, explicit convention for Cost specifically, not a reuse of an existing one, and the two sibling commands will represent cost differently by design; noted here so that divergence doesn't read as an oversight. Mixed-provider --compaction rendering: CRIT-LUMEN-188 allows --compaction with no --provider filter, so the trend set can legitimately include non-Claude-Code sessions; those sessions render an explicit n/a/absent-key marker rather than a zero-valued CompactionSummary, keeping 'zero compaction events' (Claude Code) and 'provider doesn't support compaction data' (everyone else) distinguishable. Sequence gaps from CRIT-LUMEN-192: malformed events are common in real data and get skipped rather than persisted, so a session's true last compact_boundary event in the transcript is frequently not the same as its last *persisted* event; sequence still increments for every encountered event (including skipped ones) so gaps are visible and honest, and CRIT-LUMEN-184's tokens_dropped_total is defined against the last event that WAS persisted. JSON envelope shape (round 3 fix): a bare JSON array cannot also carry the sibling anomaly_rate scalar CRIT-LUMEN-183 requires at the set level, so CRIT-LUMEN-186 now specifies an explicit object root ({"sessions": [...], "anomaly_rate": ...}), matching cmd_ingest's existing envelope-style JSON output (main.rs) rather than `lumen sessions --json`'s bare-array shape -- a deliberate divergence, stated explicitly rather than left to look like an inconsistency. compaction key presence (round 3 fix): SessionTrendPoint.compaction uses #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] so the JSON key is absent whenever there is nothing to report, rather than present as null, for both the --compaction-not-set case and the non-Claude-Code-row case. Migration idempotency (round 3 fix): MigrationManager::SCHEMA re-executes in full on every SqliteStore::open, so every existing table/index statement uses IF NOT EXISTS; the compaction_events migration now matches that convention on both the CREATE TABLE and the CREATE INDEX statements. Compaction-rendering threshold (round 3 fix): CRIT-LUMEN-184's guard was relaxed from 'at least 2 Claude Code sessions' to 'at least 1 Claude Code session present in the returned trend set' -- closing a reachable gap where exactly 1 Claude Code session mixed with other-provider sessions satisfied neither CRIT-LUMEN-187 (>= 2 sessions total), CRIT-LUMEN-188 (count > 0), nor CRIT-LUMEN-184's old 2-session floor, leaving that state's rendering undefined. A second, stricter Claude-Code-specific minimum was considered and rejected: CRIT-LUMEN-188 already covers the genuine empty case, and this spec's whole purpose is showing real per-session data as-is rather than gating it behind an additional arbitrary trend-sized minimum that only the compaction sub-view would enforce. Cache-hit-ratio/anomaly-rate scale (round 4 fix, resolved directly rather than via a 4th automated gate round per the gate's own retry-limit protocol): independently verified against crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs and crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs that sessions.cache_hit_ratio is already stored and rendered as a percentage in [0.0, 100.0] (main.rs's existing `format!("{:.1}%", ...)` applies no additional multiply) -- CRIT-LUMEN-183's original 'ratio*100.0' language and CRIT-LUMEN-186's original '[0.0, 1.0]' JSON range were both wrong relative to this real, established convention, not just internally inconsistent with each other. Resolution: keep cache_hit_ratio on its existing [0.0, 100.0] scale in both table and JSON output (no rescaling introduced), and define the new anomaly_rate value the same way -- a [0.0, 100.0] percentage, not a [0.0, 1.0] fraction -- so this spec introduces exactly one percentage convention, matching what the rest of the codebase already uses, rather than mixing two scales in one JSON payload. Both are rounded half-to-even to one decimal place before use in either mode, which also sidesteps any question about f32-to-f64 serialization precision by never emitting an unrounded value in the first place.
